note: The cast for Phase 1. Each faction's leader is its first listed member who is free in the city, so order matters. History records cite docs/research/cast-405-395.md; the fields named in 'invented' are game invention. 'enters' is the first season someone can appear (format season-year).

people.name: Dionysius
people.role: General with supreme power, tyrant of Syracuse

facts.text: Son of a Hermocrates, not the general Hermocrates whose daughter he married.
facts.quote: Dionysius, the son of Hermocrates

facts.text: Rose from clerk to tyrant.
facts.quote: from a scribe and ordinary private citizen

facts.text: The assembly made him sole general.
facts.quote: to appoint him general with supreme power

facts.text: Given a bodyguard at Leontini.
facts.quote: to give him a guard of six hundred soldiers

facts.text: Lived in the naval station before the citadel was built.
facts.quote: he took up his quarters in the naval station

people.name: Leptines
people.role: The ruler's brother; admiral of the fleet by about 397
people.rivalNote: Heir: wins commands and the guard's favour. Historically he made his own peace in Italy and was relieved of the fleet (about 390, after our period).

facts.text: Admiral by about 397.
facts.quote: he left Leptines his admiral in command of the works

facts.text: Brave but rash at the sea fight off Catana, about 396.
facts.quote: in no cowardly fashion, but without prudence

facts.text: Beaten and fled.
facts.quote: Leptines was driven off and compelled to flee to the open sea

facts.text: Later made peace in Italy on his own terms and lost the fleet (after 395).
facts.quote: to his own advantage, but without any profit to Dionysius

facts.text: Gave a daughter to Philistus without asking Dionysius (no date).
facts.quote: who had two daughters by a woman whom he had corrupted when she was living with another man and then taken to wife, gave one of them to Philistus

people.name: Thearides
people.role: The ruler's younger brother
people.rivalNote: Heir in waiting. No text gives him a role between 405 and 395; he takes the fleet after Leptines (after 395).

facts.text: Named as Dionysius' other brother and later admiral.
facts.quote: appointed Thearides, his other brother, commander of the fleet

facts.text: Later married Dionysius' daughter Arete.
facts.quote: Arete of his brother Thearides

people.name: Polyxenus
people.role: Brother-in-law of the ruler, of the house of Hermocrates; envoy
people.rivalNote: Spymaster: contacts in Italy, Sparta and Corinth. Historically he later fled Sicily as Dionysius' enemy (no date).

facts.text: Married Dionysius' sister to bind the house of Hermocrates.
facts.quote: gave his sister in marriage to Polyxenus, the brother of Hermocrates' wife

facts.text: Advised flight during the siege, about 404.
facts.quote: to use his swiftest horse and ride off

facts.text: Envoy for help, 397/396.
facts.quote: as ambassador both to the Greeks in Italy and to the Lacedaemonians, as well as the Corinthians

facts.text: Came back with a fleet.
facts.quote: bringing thirty warships from his allies

facts.text: Later fled into exile (no date).
facts.quote: moved by fear to run away and go into exile from Sicily

disputes: Polyaenus 5.2.4 names a Hermocrates as the husband of Dionysius' sister. Diodorus and Plutarch say Polyxenus.

people.name: Theste
people.role: The ruler's sister, wife of Polyxenus

facts.text: Sister of Dionysius, married to Polyxenus.
facts.quote: had a sister, Theste, whose husband, Polyxenus, had become his enemy

facts.text: When Polyxenus fled, she would not apologise for him.
facts.quote: it would have been well for me to be called the wife of Polyxenus the exile, rather than the sister of Dionysius the tyrant

disputes: Polyaenus 5.2.4 says a Hermocrates married Dionysius' sister and was banished to the Peloponnese. Diodorus and Plutarch name Polyxenus. Possibly two sisters, possibly one story told twice.

people.name: Heloris
people.role: Friend and counsellor, said by some to be the ruler's adoptive father
people.rivalNote: Enemy in waiting. Historically banished (date unknown, between about 404 and 394) and became the general of the Italian Greeks against Dionysius. An Exiled scar fits him.

facts.text: Counsellor at the siege of the Island, about 404.
facts.quote: Heloris, one of his friends, or as some say, his adopted father

facts.text: His advice to stand and die.
facts.quote: Tyranny is a fair winding-sheet

facts.text: Later banished, and trusted by the Italian Greeks for his hatred.
facts.quote: because of his hatred, to lead a war against the tyrant

facts.text: General of Rhegium by about 394.
facts.quote: their general Heloris arrived

people.name: Andron
people.role: Trusted keeper of the fortress and the treasury while the ruler is away
people.rivalNote: A loyalty test, not a rival: tempted to seize the citadel and treasury, he confessed and was executed for not reporting at once. Polyaenus gives no date.

facts.text: Left in charge of fortress and treasury, and tempted to seize them.
facts.quote: he left Andron in charge of the fortress and the treasury

facts.text: Executed for keeping quiet.
facts.quote: because he had not revealed the proposal

people.name: Doris
people.role: Daughter of Xenetus of Locri; the ruler's wife from about 398
people.entersNote: Diodorus places the marriage in about 398 (range 399 to 397)
people.rivalNote: Heir by proxy: she bore the eldest son, and her rivalry with Aristomache is in Plutarch.

facts.text: Chosen from Locri after Rhegium refused.
facts.quote: Doris, the daughter of Xenetus, who at that time was their most esteemed citizen

facts.text: Brought over on the first quinquereme.
facts.quote: a quinquereme, the first one he had built

facts.text: Bore the eldest son first.
facts.quote: Doris had the good fortune to become a mother first

facts.text: Her mother was put to death, accused of drugging Aristomache (no date).
facts.quote: accused the mother of his Locrian wife of giving Aristomache drugs to prevent conception, and put her to death

people.name: Hipparinus
people.role: Leading man of Syracuse, once Dionysius' fellow general
people.rivalNote: Kingmaker: Aristotle says he put Dionysius forward. He can climb by marrying his daughter into the ruler's house.

facts.text: Backed Dionysius' rise.
facts.quote: Hipparinus put forward Dionysius at Syracuse

facts.text: Fellow general in 406/405.
facts.quote: had been a colleague of Dionysius when he was first chosen general with full powers

people.name: Philistus
people.role: Rich backer of the tyranny, later its historian
people.rivalNote: Climber: lends, petitions, marries into the family. Historically banished for marrying Leptines' daughter without leave (no date).

facts.text: Paid Dionysius' fine in the assembly, 406/405.
facts.quote: Philistus, who later composed his History, a man of great wealth, paid the fine

facts.text: Advised against flight, about 404.
facts.quote: dragged by the leg

facts.text: Long commanded the citadel garrison.
facts.quote: for a long time was commander of the garrison that guarded the citadel

facts.text: A story of an affair with Dionysius' mother.
facts.quote: There was a story, too, that he was very intimate with the mother of the elder Dionysius

facts.text: Banished after marrying Leptines' daughter (no date).
facts.quote: banished Philistus from Sicily

people.name: Aristomache
people.role: Daughter of Hipparinus; the ruler's wife from about 398

facts.text: The most notable maiden of Syracuse.
facts.quote: the most notable maiden among them, Aristomachê

facts.text: Married on the same day as Doris.
facts.quote: he married both wives on one day

facts.text: Long childless.
facts.quote: was for a long time a barren wife

people.name: Theodorus
people.role: Cavalryman and assembly speaker for liberty
people.rivalNote: Champion: speaks for liberty in the assembly. Attested only in about 396; present from the start is a game choice.

facts.text: Respected by the cavalry.
facts.quote: Theodorus, a Syracusan, who was held in high esteem among the cavalry and was considered a man of action

facts.text: Asked Dionysius to step down, about 396.
facts.quote: if he is willing to lay down his office of his own accord, let us allow him to leave the city with his possessions

people.name: the leader of the exiles at Aetna
people.role: Commander of the exiled cavalry at Aetna (no text names him)
grudges: you burned the gate of Achradina and shot down his men in the market-place, 405
people.rivalNote: The role is history; the man is unnamed. His scar and rank are invention.

facts.text: The cavalry who resisted were killed.
facts.quote: surrounded by the mercenaries and shot down to a man

facts.text: The rest held Aetna.
facts.quote: fled from the city and occupied Aetnê

facts.text: Thousands gathered there, about 404.
facts.quote: more than seven thousand of them were gathered with the cavalry at Aetnê

people.name: the brother of Demarchus
people.role: Brother of a man you executed
grudges: you had his brother Demarchus put to death, 406/405
people.rivalNote: Invented in the paper test. Demarchus is history (Diodorus 13.96.3); no text names any kin.

people.name: Nicoteles
people.role: A Corinthian, leader of the Syracusans
people.rivalNote: Champion of the people. Historically killed by the Spartan envoy Aristus, about 404.

facts.text: A leader of the people, killed about 404.
facts.quote: slew Nicoteles the Corinthian, a leader of the Syracusans

people.name: Damon the smith
people.role: A smith who speaks for the poor in the assembly
people.rivalNote: Invented, so the people have a voice after Nicoteles. The sources name no other leader of the common citizens in these years.

people.name: Aristotle the Spartan
people.role: Commander of the mercenaries
people.rivalNote: Kingmaker: if the guard goes unpaid he leads it. Attested as commander only in about 396, when he was arrested and sent to Sparta; commanding from the start is a game choice.

facts.text: Commander of the hostile mercenaries, arrested about 396.
facts.quote: arrested Aristotle, their commander

facts.text: The mercenaries took Leontini instead of pay.
facts.quote: in lieu of their pay the city and territory of the Leontines

people.name: the captain of the guard
people.role: A captain of your mercenaries
people.rivalNote: Invented in the paper test. No text names the guard's captain in 405 (Diodorus 13.96.1 names nobody). Aristotle the Spartan is the attested commander by about 396; the engine may use one or the other.

people.name: Doricus
people.role: Your officer, set over the citizen soldiers
people.rivalNote: Loyalist. Historically killed by his own soldiers at Herbessus, about 404.

facts.text: Appointed commander; killed by the citizen soldiers he struck at, about 404.
facts.quote: slew the commander, whose name was Doricus

people.name: Biton
people.role: A Syracusan garrison commander

facts.text: Put in charge of the garrison at Motya, about 397.
facts.quote: under the command of Biton of Syracuse

people.name: Archylus of Thurii
people.role: Leader of the picked troops

facts.text: First over the wall at Motya, about 397.
facts.quote: who had been the first to mount the wall, with one hundred minas

people.name: the daughter of Hermocrates
people.role: The ruler's first wife

facts.text: Married at the start of the tyranny.
facts.quote: Dionysius straightway married the daughter of Hermocrates

disputes: Diodorus 14.44.5: she was "slain at the time the cavalry revolted".
Plutarch, Dion 3: she was abused by the rebels "and in consequence put an end to her own life".

people.name: Daphnaeus
people.role: Former general, executed 405

facts.text: General for the relief of Acragas.
facts.quote: they elected Daphnaeus general

facts.text: Executed.
facts.quote: his most influential opponents, Daphnaeus and Demarchus, put to death

people.name: Demarchus
people.role: Opponent of the ruler, executed 405

facts.text: Executed.
facts.quote: his most influential opponents, Daphnaeus and Demarchus, put to death
